title: Early Osteogenic and Stromal Marker Responses of Osteoblast -like and Bone - Marrow Stromal Cell Lines to a Hyaluronic Acid -Coated Xenogeneic Bone Graft: An Exploratory In Vitro Analysis
authors: Mayer, Y.; Abu Sada, H.; Zigdon Giladi, H.; Gabay, E.; Doppelt -Flikshtain, O.; Ginesin, O. Dent J (Basel). 2026 May 12;14(5):290. doi: 10.3390/dj14050290.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone plus (bovine bone with hyaluronate) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “These exploratory in vitro findings suggest that HA coating may enhance early osteogenic marker expression. The observed effects on stromal markers warrant further investigation using primary cells, additional fibrotic endpoints (e.g., TGF-β1, ACTA2), and in vivo models before translational conclusions can be drawn. 3” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
